additional_requirements: The binge eating and inappropriate compensatory behaviors both occur, on average, at least once a week for 3 months

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.

subtypes.Self-Induced Vomiting: Intentionally inducing vomiting to remove ingested food.
subtypes.Misuse of Medications: Repetitively misusing laxatives, diuretics, or enemas for the purpose of weight control.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
examples: Eating more than 3-4 times the amount of a typical meal within 2 hours.
Continuously eating large amounts of high-calorie snacks in addition to main meals.
Eating enough to empty a significant portion of the refrigerator or pantry at once.
Eating clearly more food than others during the same period of time.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
examples: A feeling that once I start eating, I cannot stop even if I want to.
Thinking 'I shouldn't eat any more' but mechanically continuing to eat.
A feeling of helplessness that I cannot decide for myself how much to eat.
Eating as if my body is being controlled by someone else.

symptom.disease_info: Bulimia Nervosa is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts of food with a sense of loss of control, followed by compensatory behaviors such as self-induced purging, with self-evaluation strongly tied to weight or shape. It often develops over months to years, may be hidden because weight can remain in a socially expected range, and is distinguished from anorexia nervosa by the absence of persistently significantly low body weight as the defining feature.

patient.stressor: Bobby’s symptoms began after he started college and lost the predictable structure of home meals, outdoor routines, and familiar Lexington friendships. During the following 7 months, the combination of dining-hall access, late-night studying, and quiet isolation made episodes of eating unusually large amounts feel increasingly out of his control, while his self-worth became tied to whether he thought he looked lean enough compared with other students. He began purging repeatedly to counteract the eating episodes, and the cycle became frequent enough that he stopped trusting himself around food and avoided situations where eating might be noticed. He sought psychiatric care through the campus counseling service after completing an online student health screening and recognizing that the pattern matched a serious eating disorder rather than a temporary adjustment problem.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: I can have a decent day in classes, but if I catch my reflection in a dorm window and think my stomach or face looks bigger than the guys around me, it feels like I failed at everything and I don't want anyone to see me.

S048.name: Compensatory_Behavior_Purging
S048.description: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors involving the expulsion of food or fluids to prevent weight gain.
S048.manifestation: After I eat like that, I usually end up in a bathroom in the dorm or a quiet floor of the library making myself throw up because I feel terrified that the food is just sitting there turning into weight.

S049.name: Eating_Large_Amount
S049.description: Eating, in a discrete period of time, an amount of food that is definitely larger than what most individuals would eat in a similar period of time under similar circumstances.
S049.manifestation: There have been nights after studying where I go from the dining hall to my room and eat burgers, cereal, peanut butter, snacks, whatever I can get, way more than a normal dinner, until the trash is full and I feel sick.

S050.name: Loss_of_Control
S050.description: A sense of lack of control over eating during the episode (e.g., a feeling that one cannot stop eating or control what or how much one is eating).
S050.manifestation: I came in because once I start eating, it feels like I disappear and something else takes over, and even while I'm telling myself to stop, I keep going until I can't stand it anymore.

add_requirements.binge_eating_and_inappropriate_compensat: For most of this semester, the eating episodes and throwing up have been happening several times a week, not just once in a while. I can look back over at least the last few months and there really hasn’t been a week where the cycle stopped.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’ve stopped going to a lot of meals or hangouts with people from my dorm because I’m scared they’ll notice how I act around food. My studying has also gotten messier because whole nights get taken over by planning around eating or trying to recover afterward.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about seven months, starting after I came to college and my normal home routine disappeared.
